question.text: Under SEBI AIF Regulations (Regulation 16 and 17), Cat I and Cat II AIFs:

answer.text: May leverage up to 2x NAV (like Cat III).
Must invest only in listed equity.
May NOT borrow funds for making investments directly or indirectly (except for temporary funding needs up to 30 days, 10% of corpus, max 4 times a year).
Must provide monthly NAV to investors.

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulations 16 (Cat I) and 17 (Cat II) prohibit Cat I/II AIFs from leveraging or borrowing for investment. Temporary borrowings for short-term funding needs (30 days, 10% of corpus, max 4 times a year) are permitted. The Trap: 2x NAV leverage is the Cat III rule. 'Only listed equity' is false. Monthly NAV is Cat III open-ended rule. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-E Cat III will test 2x leverage. XIX-D must know the Cat I/II prohibition cold. Manager's Pro-Tip: Plan cash-flow carefully - since Cat I/II can't lever, mistimed drawdowns can force asset sales or bridge funding. Negotiate LP consent for a 30-day bridge-loan facility in advance.
